questions.explanation: About 3 seconds before is the timing for changing lanes while travelling in the same direction. The signal for a right or left turn is given on reaching the point 30 metres before that intersection (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1)).
questions.question: For a right or left turn at an intersection it is enough to signal (by indicator or hand) about 3 seconds before entering that intersection.

questions.explanation: About 3 seconds before is the timing for changing lanes while travelling in the same direction. The signal for a U-turn is given on reaching the point 30 metres before the place where you intend to turn (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1)).
questions.question: The signal (by indicator or hand) for a U-turn is given about 3 seconds before the turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(1). The same goes for reversing and for turning or crossing in order to enter or leave a roadside facility.
questions.question: Even where no road sign or road marking forbids it, a vehicle may not cross the road or make a U-turn when doing so might obstruct pedestrians or the normal passage of other vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1). The same applies to reversing: the safety check comes first and the signal second.
questions.question: Before changing lanes or making a U-turn, you must first check that it is safe in the rear-view mirror and the like, and only then signal (by indicator or hand).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1). You must not change course without good reason.
questions.question: When changing course you must check the direction you are moving into and the road behind, in the rear-view mirror and with your own eyes, and you must not change course when a vehicle coming up behind would have to brake hard or swerve to avoid you.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(4). A vehicle turning left to leave the road moves over to the left edge in advance and one turning right moves to the centre, or to the right edge on a one-way road, and both proceed slowly (徐行).
questions.question: When the vehicle in front is signalling (by indicator or hand) that it is moving over to the left edge, the centre or the right edge of the road in order to leave the road, you must not obstruct its change of course, unless you would have to brake hard or swerve to avoid it.

questions.explanation: Turning is not one of the exceptions. You may cross the yellow line to change lanes when you are giving way to an emergency vehicle, or when damage to the road, road works or another obstruction stops you using that lane (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2); Road Traffic Act Article 26-2 paragraph 3).
questions.question: Even where vehicle lanes are divided by a yellow line, you may cross that line to change lanes if you are doing so in order to turn right or left.

questions.explanation: Where that sign stands you may not make a U-turn, whatever the other traffic is doing. What the risk of obstructing other traffic forbids is crossing and turning where no sign or marking forbids it (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 items 3(1) and 3(2)).
questions.question: Even where there is a "No U-turn" road sign, you may make a U-turn when there is no risk of obstructing other traffic.

questions.explanation: The absence of a vehicle behind is not an exception to this prohibition. You may cross only when you are giving way to an emergency vehicle, or when damage to the road, road works or another obstruction stops you using that lane (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2); Road Traffic Act Article 26-2 paragraph 3).
questions.question: Even where vehicle lanes are divided by a yellow line, you may cross it to change lanes when there is no vehicle coming up behind.

questions.explanation: When damage to the road, road works or another obstruction stops you using that vehicle lane, you may cross the yellow line to change lanes. The same goes for giving way to an emergency vehicle (Road Traffic Act Article 26-2 paragraph 3; Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2)).
questions.question: Where vehicle lanes are divided by a yellow line, you may not cross the yellow line to change lanes even when an obstruction such as road works stops you using that lane.

questions.explanation: Those signs forbid a vehicle from crossing the road and from making a U-turn, and reversing is not included (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 13 and 14). What you may not do where a sign or marking forbids something is the act it forbids (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(2)).
questions.question: Where there is a "No crossing for vehicles" or "No U-turn" road sign, reversing is forbidden as well as crossing and U-turns.

questions.explanation: When you move to the left or the right of the road to give way to an emergency vehicle, you may cross the yellow line to change lanes (Road Traffic Act Article 26-2 paragraph 3 item 1). That case is laid down as an exception to the ban on changing lanes (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2)).
questions.question: When an emergency vehicle comes up from behind with its siren on, a vehicle moving to the left of the road is not allowed to go so far as to cross the yellow line dividing the vehicle lanes and change lanes.

questions.explanation: You must check that it is safe and signal as well. The signal for changing lanes is given about 3 seconds before the change (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1)).
questions.question: When changing course, as long as you have checked behind you in the rear-view mirror and with your own eyes, there is no need to signal (by indicator or hand).

questions.explanation: The order is the wrong way round. You must first check that it is safe in the rear-view mirror and the like, and only then signal (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1)).
questions.question: When you are about to change lanes or make a U-turn, you signal (by indicator or hand) first and then check behind you in the rear-view mirror and the like.

questions.explanation: Where the lanes are divided by a yellow line, you may not cross it to change lanes. A slow vehicle in front is not an exception to that prohibition (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2)).
questions.question: Driving on a road with two lanes in your direction, the vehicle in front was slow, so you crossed the yellow line dividing the vehicle lanes and moved into the next lane.

questions.explanation: You may not change course where the vehicle coming up behind would have to brake hard or swerve to avoid you. Wait until there is enough distance between you and the vehicle behind (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(1)).
questions.question: A vehicle coming up behind was already very close, but you judged that a quick turn of the wheel would get you across in time, so you changed into the next vehicle lane.

questions.explanation: Where the lanes are divided by a white line you may change lanes. What you may not do is change lanes where they are divided by a yellow line, or where a yellow line runs alongside on the side of the lane you are in (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2)).
questions.question: Where vehicle lanes are divided by a white line, a vehicle may not change lanes.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 2. A yellow line shows that crossing into the right-hand part of the road to overtake is forbidden.
questions.question: Where the centre line of the road is shown by a yellow line, a vehicle must not cross into the right-hand part of the road to overtake.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) part C. These are also places where you must proceed slowly (徐行), and you may not overtake even if the vehicle ahead is slow.
questions.question: Near the crest of a hill and on a steep downgrade are places where you may not change course to overtake a motor vehicle or a general motorized bicycle (moped), nor pass along its side.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) part B. Near a bend is a no-overtaking place whatever the state of the road and the visibility, and it is also a place where you must proceed slowly (徐行).
questions.question: Near a bend in the road is a place where overtaking is forbidden, whether visibility is good or not.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) part F. A pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing and the 30 metres before it are no-overtaking places in the same way.
questions.question: At a railway crossing and within 30 metres before it, you may not change course to overtake a motor vehicle or a general motorized bicycle (moped), nor pass along its side.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) part E. What is excepted is an intersection on the priority road while you are travelling on that priority road (Road Traffic Act Article 30 item 3).
questions.question: At an intersection and within 30 metres before it, overtaking is forbidden except where you are travelling on a priority road.

questions.explanation: A stop and the space before and after it are not no-overtaking places. Overtaking is forbidden where there is a sign, near a bend in the road, near the crest of a hill and on a steep downgrade, in a tunnel without vehicle lanes, and at an intersection, a railway crossing, a pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing and within 30 metres before it (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)).
questions.question: A bus stop and the 30 metres before and after it are places where overtaking is forbidden.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3). What is forbidden there is overtaking a motor vehicle or a general motorized bicycle (moped); light road vehicles are not covered.
questions.question: Even in a place where overtaking is forbidden, you may overtake a light road vehicle (bicycle, cart, etc.) such as a bicycle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3). In a no-overtaking place neither a motor vehicle nor a general motorized bicycle may be overtaken.
questions.question: In a place where overtaking is forbidden, you may not overtake a general motorized bicycle (moped) either, not only a motor vehicle.

questions.explanation: A steep downgrade is a no-overtaking place. Even if the vehicle ahead is slow and even if there is no oncoming vehicle, you may not overtake a general motorized bicycle (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3) part C).
questions.question: On a steep downgrade, because the general motorized bicycle (moped) ahead was slow, the driver checked that there was no oncoming vehicle and overtook it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2) part A. What you must not begin is overtaking while the vehicle ahead is about to overtake a motor vehicle.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead is about to overtake a general motorized bicycle (moped), that is not double overtaking, so you may overtake that vehicle unless something else forbids overtaking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2) part A. This is called double overtaking, and Article 29 of the Road Traffic Act forbids it as well.
questions.question: A driver must not attempt to overtake the vehicle running ahead while that vehicle is itself about to overtake another motor vehicle.

questions.explanation: While the vehicle ahead is about to overtake a motor vehicle, you must not begin to overtake. Even with a clear road ahead, double overtaking is not allowed (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2) part A).
questions.question: Even while the vehicle ahead is overtaking a motor vehicle, you may overtake both vehicles at once as long as the road ahead of them is clear enough.

questions.explanation: When overtaking you pass on the vehicle's right as a rule. You pass on the left when the vehicle ahead has moved to the centre of the road (to the right edge on a one-way road) in order to turn right, and when overtaking a streetcar (tram) (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1)).
questions.question: A driver who is going to overtake must pass on the left of the vehicle ahead and come out in front of it.

questions.explanation: While overtaking you must keep a safe interval from the vehicle you are overtaking. Closing up the following distance risks a rear-end collision and makes it harder to see what is ahead (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(2)).
questions.question: I closed right up on the vehicle ahead and then overtook it, squeezing past its side with barely any gap.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 5(2). When passing an oncoming vehicle, the rule is that the vehicle on the side where the obstacle is gives way to the oncoming vehicle.
questions.question: When you pass an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road and the obstacle, such as a parked vehicle, is on your own side, come to a complete stop (一時停止) or slow down in advance and give way to the oncoming vehicle.

questions.explanation: It is the other way round. The vehicle on the side where the obstacle is comes to a complete stop (一時停止) or slows down in advance and gives way to the vehicle coming from the opposite direction (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 5(2)).
questions.question: When there is an obstacle ahead on your course, the vehicle on the side where the obstacle is may go first, and the vehicle coming from the opposite direction must give way.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1). Overtaking on the right is the rule, and these two are the cases where it is done on the left.
questions.question: When overtaking another vehicle you must pass on its right, but when the vehicle ahead has moved to the centre of the road (to the right edge on a one-way road) to turn right, and when overtaking a streetcar (tram), you pass on its left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(1). On a one-way road, when the vehicle ahead has moved to the right edge to turn right, you pass on its left in the same way.
questions.question: When the vehicle ahead is travelling close to the centre of the road in order to turn right, you overtake it by passing on its left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 items 3(2) and 3(3). When the overtaking will take you across into the right-hand side of the road, also check that the opposite direction is clear.
questions.question: When overtaking, check that it is safe ahead and check the right side and the right rear diagonal with the mirrors, and only then switch on the right turn indicator.

questions.explanation: The order is reversed. You check that it is safe ahead and check the right side and the right rear diagonal with the mirrors, and then switch on the right turn indicator (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 items 3(2) and 3(3)).
questions.question: When overtaking, first switch on the right turn indicator and only after that check that it is safe ahead and to the right rear diagonal.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3(4). About 3 seconds after switching on the right turn indicator, you move gently to the right while accelerating within the maximum speed limit.
questions.question: Overtaking requires you to accelerate, but even then you must not drive above the maximum speed for that road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3(6). Before that you switch on the left turn indicator, and you stop signalling (by indicator or hand) once you have moved back.
questions.question: When you come back to the left after overtaking, go on until the vehicle you overtook can be seen in the rear-view mirror and only then move gently to the left.

questions.explanation: You go on until the vehicle you overtook can be seen in the rear-view mirror and then move gently to the left. Cutting in just in front forces the overtaken vehicle to brake hard (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 3(6)).
questions.question: Once you have finished overtaking, it is best to cut in quickly just in front of the vehicle you overtook.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 4. When the vehicle ahead is stopped or proceeding slowly at an intersection, a railway crossing or the like, you must not cut in front of it or cross in front of it (Road Traffic Act Article 32).
questions.question: When you catch up with a vehicle that is proceeding slowly (徐行) because it is about to stop in order to avoid danger, you must not cut in in front of it.

questions.explanation: It is precisely when there is not enough room to overtake that you must move as far to the left as you can and give way (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(4)).
questions.question: Even when a vehicle behind is trying to overtake, you need not give way if there is not enough room for it to overtake.

questions.explanation: Where there is not enough room to overtake, you must move as far to the left as you can and give way. Also, while you are being overtaken you must not increase speed until the overtaking is finished (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 2(4)).
questions.question: A vehicle behind was trying to overtake, but because there was not enough room for it to overtake, the driver stayed at the same speed without moving to the left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 items 5(1) and 5(2). So that the two vehicles pass each other where there is no obstacle, let the oncoming vehicle through first when the obstacle is ahead in your own path.
questions.question: When passing an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, keep a safe interval, and when there is an obstacle ahead in your path, come to a complete stop (一時停止) or slow down beforehand and give way to the vehicle coming the other way.

questions.explanation: The 30 metres is when the signal (by indicator or hand) starts. You must move over to the left edge of the road as far as possible in advance (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1) and Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(1)).
questions.question: When a vehicle turns left, it is enough to move over to the left edge of the road after reaching the point 30 metres before the place where it will turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(8). The same applies to a vehicle signalling in order to move into the vehicle lane designated by a road sign or road marking.
questions.question: When the vehicle in front signals (by indicator or hand) that it is changing course in order to turn right, you must not obstruct its change of course, unless you would have to brake hard or swerve to avoid it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1). Moving to the left edge beforehand keeps you from catching a bicycle or the like travelling on your left.
questions.question: A driver who is about to turn left at an intersection must bring the vehicle as close to the left edge of the road as possible beforehand and turn while proceeding slowly (徐行) along the edge of the intersection.

questions.explanation: That is the method for a right turn. For a left turn you move as close to the left edge of the road as you can beforehand and proceed slowly along the edge of the intersection (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 items 2(1) and 2(2)).
questions.question: When you are going to make a left turn, you move as close to the centre of the road as you can beforehand and proceed slowly (徐行) just inside the centre of the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(2). A general motorized bicycle making a two-step right turn moves to the left edge of the road beforehand.
questions.question: When you are going to make a right turn, you must move as close to the centre of the road as you can beforehand and proceed slowly (徐行) just inside the centre of the intersection. This does not apply to a general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(3). A one-way road has no oncoming traffic, so you move to the right edge rather than to the centre.
questions.question: When turning right from a one-way road, you must move as close to the right edge of the road as you can beforehand and proceed slowly (徐行) inside the centre of the intersection. This does not apply to a general motorized bicycle (moped) making a two-step right turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5). Whether you entered the intersection first makes no difference (Road Traffic Act Article 37).
questions.question: A vehicle turning right at an intersection must not obstruct the progress of vehicles or streetcars (trams) going straight through or turning left there, even if it entered the intersection first.

questions.explanation: Even having entered the intersection first, you must not obstruct the progress of vehicles or streetcars (trams) going straight through or turning left. You turn right after they have passed (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(5)).
questions.question: When turning right at an intersection, if your vehicle entered the intersection first you may turn without waiting for a vehicle coming straight on in the oncoming lane.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3). The larger the vehicle, the larger the inner wheel difference.
questions.question: When a vehicle turns a corner the rear wheels pass inside the front wheels, so a gap opens between the paths of the front and rear wheels; that gap is called the inner wheel difference.

questions.explanation: Front and rear are the wrong way round. It is the rear wheels that pass inside, and that gap in their paths is the inner wheel difference (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3)).
questions.question: The inner wheel difference is the gap between the paths of the front and rear wheels that arises because the front wheels pass inside the rear wheels when a vehicle turns.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3). Large-sized motor vehicles in particular have a big inner wheel difference and poor visibility to the left rear, so extra care is needed.
questions.question: When turning left you must take care that the inner wheel difference does not catch a pedestrian or a bicycle travelling on your left.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3). It arises whenever a vehicle turns right or left, so watch out for catching someone on a right turn too.
questions.question: The inner wheel difference arises not only when turning left but also when turning right.

questions.explanation: The inner wheel difference arises whenever a vehicle turns and does not disappear because you proceed slowly. When turning left, watch out for catching pedestrians and bicycles travelling on your left (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(3)).
questions.question: If you turn while proceeding slowly (徐行) no inner wheel difference arises, so on a left turn there is no need to worry about pedestrians on the left.

questions.explanation: For a left turn you move as close to the left edge of the road as you can beforehand and proceed slowly (徐行) along the edge of the intersection. Swinging out to the right first puts the vehicles behind and the oncoming traffic in danger (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(1)).
questions.question: When turning left it is a good idea to steer to the right once in order to remove the inner wheel difference, and then make the turn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9). The same goes for a place with the No stopping zone marking and for a pedestrian crossing or railway crossing where you might end up unable to move.
questions.question: When congested traffic ahead means you might end up stopped inside the intersection and obstruct the traffic crossing it, you must not enter the intersection even on a green light.

questions.explanation: When there is a risk of stopping inside the intersection and obstructing the traffic crossing it, you must not enter even on a green light. You stop before it and wait (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(9)).
questions.question: Because the light was green, the driver entered the intersection anyway and came to a stop, although congested traffic ahead meant there was a risk of being stopped inside it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1). This duty to proceed slowly does not apply while you are travelling on a priority road yourself (Road Traffic Act Article 36(3)).
questions.question: When you come up to an intersection with neither a traffic light nor a police officer directing traffic, and the crossing road is a priority road or is wider, you must proceed slowly (徐行) and keep from obstructing the progress of the vehicles and streetcars (trams) travelling on that road.

questions.explanation: When the crossing road is a priority road you must proceed slowly, whether or not there is a vehicle on it (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1), Road Traffic Act Article 36(3)).
questions.question: When you are about to enter a priority road at an intersection where no traffic control is in operation, you may go on without proceeding slowly (徐行) if no vehicle can be seen travelling on that priority road.

questions.explanation: When the crossing road is a priority road you must proceed slowly, whether visibility is good or bad. You must also not obstruct the progress of the vehicles and streetcars (trams) travelling on that road (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1)).
questions.question: At an intersection where no traffic control is in operation, even when the crossing road is a priority road, you may go through without proceeding slowly (徐行) if visibility to left and right is good.

questions.explanation: What is required is to proceed slowly (徐行). You must come to a complete stop where there is a Stop sign or a flashing red light (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 items 3(1) and 3(3)).
questions.question: When you are going to enter a priority road from a narrow road, even at an intersection where no traffic control is in operation, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) before it and only then go on.

questions.explanation: An intersection and its surroundings are where accidents are most frequent, and you must watch for right-turning vehicles and pedestrians and proceed at the safest speed and in the safest manner the situation allows. Judge and act with consideration for others rather than putting yourself first (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1), Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(1)).
questions.question: An intersection is a place where accidents are frequent, and giving way to other vehicles disturbs the flow, so it is best to put your own course first and go on.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(2). For streetcars you must not obstruct their progress whether or not they come from the left (Road Traffic Act Article 36(1)).
questions.question: At an intersection of roads of roughly the same width, a vehicle must not obstruct the progress of vehicles and streetcars (trams) coming from the left.

questions.explanation: Left and right are the wrong way round. At an intersection of roads of roughly the same width you must not obstruct the progress of the vehicle coming from the left (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(2), Road Traffic Act Article 36(1)).
questions.question: At an intersection of roads of roughly the same width, the vehicle coming from the right has priority, so the vehicle coming from the left must not obstruct its progress.

questions.explanation: This is Article 36(2) of the Road Traffic Act. Besides roads designated as priority roads by a sign, a road carrying those lines through the intersection is a priority road as well.
questions.question: A road on which the centre line or vehicle lanes are drawn right through the intersection is a priority road even without a priority road sign.

questions.explanation: Besides roads designated by a sign, a road with a centre line or vehicle lanes drawn through the intersection is a priority road as well. In that case you must proceed slowly (徐行) and must not obstruct the progress of the vehicles travelling on the crossing road (Road Traffic Act Article 36(2)).
questions.question: At an intersection where no traffic control is in operation, even if the crossing road has its centre line drawn right through the intersection, that road is not a priority road unless there is a priority road sign.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 4(1). You must also proceed slowly when entering a roundabout and must not obstruct the progress of the vehicles and streetcars (trams) already travelling in it (same section, item 4(3)).
questions.question: At a roundabout, even when you are turning right or making a U-turn, you must move as close to the left edge of the road as you can beforehand and proceed slowly (徐行) along its edge.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1). When entering or passing through an intersection you must proceed at as safe a speed and in as safe a manner as the situation allows, keeping an eye on right-turning vehicles, pedestrians and others.
questions.question: When turning right at an intersection, a two-wheeled vehicle (motorcycles and general motorized bicycles) coming straight on can be hard to see behind an oncoming vehicle, so even after a gap opens in the oncoming traffic, check carefully behind it before turning.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 1(1). A vehicle on the crossing road is obliged to come to a complete stop just before the stop line (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(3)), but it will not necessarily obey the sign, so you must proceed at as safe a speed and in as safe a manner as the situation allows.
questions.question: Approaching an intersection not under traffic control I saw that the crossing road had a Stop (一時停止) sign, but since a vehicle coming from that road might not stop, I entered the intersection proceeding slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(2)(i). You confirm where the pedals are by feel and by eye before starting.
questions.question: In an automatic transmission vehicle (AT), before starting the engine you press the brake pedal to confirm where it is and look at the accelerator pedal to confirm its position.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(3). The higher the engine speed, the more the brake matters before you touch the change lever.
questions.question: Just after the engine is started, and while the air conditioner is in use, an automatic transmission vehicle (AT) runs at a high engine speed and leaps forward easily, so keep the brake pedal pressed harder than usual.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4). If the stop looks like being a long one, put the change lever in N.
questions.question: While an automatic transmission vehicle (AT) is stopped, keep the brake pedal pressed firmly so that the creep phenomenon (クリープ) does not set the car moving.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(4). If you do not notice it, it can cause an unexpected accident such as a rear-end collision.
questions.question: The creep phenomenon (クリープ) is when an automatic transmission vehicle (AT) starts to move slowly without the accelerator pedal being pressed, because the brake pedal is not being held down firmly.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(5). Do not put the change lever in P before the car has come to a standstill.
questions.question: When you park an automatic transmission vehicle (AT), whether on an uphill, a downhill or level ground, press the brake pedal, set the hand brake firmly and then put the change lever in P.

questions.explanation: Not R. In an automatic transmission vehicle the change lever is left in P (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(5) and Chapter 5 Section 8 item 10(1)(ii)).
questions.question: When you stop an automatic transmission vehicle (AT) and park it, you set the hand brake firmly and then leave the change lever in the R position.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 8 item 10(1)(ii). You also stop the engine and apply the hand brake, and on a slope you use wheel chocks.
questions.question: When you leave the vehicle, in a manual transmission vehicle (MT) you put the gear in reverse on level ground or a downhill and in low gear on an uphill, and in an automatic transmission vehicle (AT) you put the change lever in P.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(1). At a railway crossing with no traffic light you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) just before it, or just before the stop line where there is one, and check that it is safe to left and right with your own eyes and ears.
questions.question: At a railway crossing with a traffic light, you may go across in accordance with that light.

questions.explanation: You must not cross. While the alarm is ringing, or the barrier is down or coming down, you must not enter the crossing (Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(3)).
questions.question: The alarm at a railway crossing started to ring, but no train was in sight yet, so you hurried across the crossing.

questions.explanation: You must not wait and see. When your vehicle will not move at a crossing, use the push-button crossing emergency alarm fitted to the alarm post or similar, so that the train driver is told as soon as possible (Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 2(1)).
questions.question: Your car would not move inside a railway crossing, but since no train was approaching you waited a while to see what happened instead of pressing the crossing emergency alarm button.

questions.explanation: This marking forbids stopping as well as parking. The marking that forbids only parking is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 4 and 5).
questions.question: Where this road marking is, parking is not allowed, but stopping to let someone in or out is.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 5. This marking forbids only parking; stopping is not forbidden.
questions.question: Where this road marking is, parking is not allowed but stopping is.

questions.explanation: This marking forbids only parking. The marking that forbids both is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 4 and 5).
questions.question: This road marking shows that both parking and stopping are forbidden.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 7. A No entry zone is a part designated as one that vehicles must not enter.
questions.question: This road marking shows a part of the road that vehicles must not drive on.

questions.explanation: A No entry zone is a part that vehicles must not drive on, so you may not drive through it either (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 7).
questions.question: You may drive through the part marked by this road marking, but you may not stop inside it.

questions.explanation: This is the No entry zone. The No stopping zone is a part you must not enter when congestion means you might end up stopped inside it, and it is a different marking (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 7 and 8).
questions.question: The part marked by this road marking is one that vehicles must not enter only when congested traffic means they might end up stopped inside it.

questions.explanation: This is the No entry zone. The safety zone marking has a yellow outer frame and a white inner frame and is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 7 and 34).
questions.question: The part with this road marking is a place for people getting on and off a streetcar (tram) to wait.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 8. It is laid in places such as in front of a police station or a fire station.
questions.question: This road marking shows a part that vehicles must not enter when traffic is congested and going on would risk leaving them stopped inside it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 8. If you might end up stopped there, wait before the marked part.
questions.question: Even while waiting for a light, you must not stop inside the part shown by this road marking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 2(9). The same goes for a pedestrian crossing or a railway crossing where you might end up unable to move.
questions.question: A vehicle must not enter the part marked by this road marking, laid in places such as in front of a police station or a fire station, when the traffic ahead is congested and going on might leave it stopped inside.

questions.explanation: You must not enter when congestion means you might end up stopped inside it. If there is no such risk you may drive through (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 8).
questions.question: A vehicle must never, under any circumstances, enter the part shown by this road marking.

questions.explanation: This is the No stopping zone. The No entry zone is a part that vehicles must not drive on, and it is a different marking (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 7 and 8).
questions.question: Whether or not the traffic is congested, vehicles must not drive on the part marked by this road marking.

questions.explanation: This is the No stopping zone. A safety zone is a place for the safety of people boarding or leaving a streetcar (tram) and of pedestrians crossing, and its marking is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 8 and 34).
questions.question: The part with this road marking is a place where pedestrians crossing the road may stand still for safety.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 8 item 3(3). A side strip marked with a solid and a broken white line is a no-stopping-or-parking side strip, and you may not enter it however wide it is.
questions.question: In the side strip (路側帯) with this road marking, a vehicle may not go inside it to park or stop.

questions.explanation: Leaving 0.75 metres or more lets you enter an ordinary side strip that is wide enough. A side strip marked with a solid and a broken white line may not be entered however wide it is (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 8 item 3(3)).
questions.question: Where the side strip (路側帯) with this road marking is wide, you may go inside it to park or stop as long as you leave 0.75 metres or more clear.

questions.explanation: This is a no-stopping-or-parking side strip. A pedestrian-only side strip is shown by two solid white lines, and light road vehicles may not pass along it either (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 10 and 11).
questions.question: Inside the side strip (路側帯) shown by this road marking, not only stopping and parking but also the passage of light road vehicles (bicycle, cart, etc.) is forbidden.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 11. In a pedestrian-only side strip, special specified small motorized bicycles and light road vehicles (bicycles, carts, etc.) are also forbidden.
questions.question: In the side strip (路側帯) with this road marking, parking and stopping are forbidden and light road vehicles may not pass along it either.

questions.explanation: This is a pedestrian-only side strip. A no-stopping-or-parking side strip is shown by a solid and a broken white line, and light road vehicles are not forbidden there (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 10 and 11).
questions.question: In the side strip (路側帯) with this road marking only stopping and parking are forbidden, and light road vehicles (bicycle, cart, etc.) may pass along it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 18. It shows the part of the intersection a turning vehicle is to follow.
questions.question: This road marking shows how a vehicle is to travel when turning right or left at an intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 28. It is the right-side travel marking, laid where an exception to keeping left is allowed.
questions.question: While driving where this road marking is laid, the driver may travel out onto the part of the road to the right of the centre.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 34. It is shown with a yellow outer frame and a white inner frame.
questions.question: The place with this road marking is where people waiting for a streetcar (tram) and people crossing the road can stand clear of vehicles, that is, a safety zone.

questions.explanation: This is a safety zone. The No entry zone is marked with a yellow edge line and white diagonal stripes, and is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) items 7 and 34).
questions.question: The part with this road marking is not a place for pedestrians but the No entry zone, which shows that vehicles must not drive there.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 38. It is laid on the road surface before a pedestrian crossing or bicycle crossing.
questions.question: While driving where this road marking is laid, the driver can tell that there is a pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: It is advance warning of a pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing ahead (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 38).
questions.question: A driver travelling where this road marking is laid may take it that there is an intersection ahead.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 39. Where the crossing road is a priority road you must proceed slowly (徐行) and must not obstruct the vehicles travelling on it.
questions.question: A vehicle coming along the road with this road marking can tell in advance that the road it will cross ahead is the priority road.

questions.explanation: It is the marking that shows the crossing road ahead is a priority road (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 39).
questions.question: This road marking does no more than tell the driver that there is an intersection ahead.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 9. On an ordinary side strip, shown by a single solid white line, a light road vehicle may pass at a speed and in a manner that does not obstruct the progress of pedestrians (Road Traffic Act Article 17-3).
questions.question: On the side strip (路側帯) with this road marking, pedestrians may walk, and light road vehicles (bicycles, carts, etc.) may also pass along it except where doing so would seriously obstruct pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Small-sized special motor vehicles, motorized bicycles and light road vehicles (bicycles, carts, etc.) may use that lane. What may not use it is every other vehicle (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 15 and Chapter 5, Section 2, item 6(2)).
questions.question: During the hours in which this road marking designates an exclusive lane for route buses, etc., a general motorized bicycle (moped) may not travel in that lane either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 16 together with Chapter 5, Section 2, item 6(3). This is a priority lane and, unlike an exclusive lane, travelling in it is not forbidden as such.
questions.question: Even during the hours in which this road marking designates a priority lane for route buses, etc., an ordinary motor vehicle may travel in that lane as long as no route bus is approaching from behind. However, when the traffic is congested so that you might be unable to leave once one approaches, you must not enter it in the first place.

questions.explanation: This marking shows a priority lane for route buses, etc., and other motor vehicles may travel in it as well. It is enough to leave it promptly when a route bus approaches from behind (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 16 and Chapter 5, Section 2, item 6(3)).
questions.question: During the hours designated by this road marking, motor vehicles other than route buses, etc. may not travel in that lane.

questions.explanation: A school bus is counted among route buses, etc., so when one approaches from behind you must promptly leave that lane (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 16 and Road Traffic Act Article 20-2(1)).
questions.question: While travelling during the designated hours in the lane carrying this road marking, if what is approaching from behind is a school bus (school / kindergarten bus), you do not have to leave the lane.

questions.explanation: This marking shows the part of the road you must use when turning right or left, and it does not mean you may skip proceeding slowly. When you turn right you must pass just inside the centre of the intersection and go slowly (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 18 and Chapter 5 Section 7 item 2(2)).
questions.question: At an intersection with this road marking, you need not proceed slowly (徐行) when turning right as long as you follow the marking.

questions.explanation: This marking forbids changing lanes, and where the lanes are divided by solid yellow lines on both sides a vehicle in either lane may not change lanes. Neither A to B nor B to A is allowed (Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 3 and Chapter 5 Section 5 item 2(2)).
questions.question: In the vehicle lanes divided by this road marking, a vehicle in lane A may change into lane B.

questions.explanation: This is the "Left turn permitted" plate. It shows that you may turn left while paying attention to the traffic around you, even when the light ahead is red or yellow (Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4)).
questions.question: The road with this sign plate is one way, and a vehicle may travel only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 3. It is placed at the exit of a one-way street and similar places.
questions.question: Vehicles must not enter from that direction where this sign stands.

questions.explanation: This is No entry for vehicles. What is forbidden is only entry from the direction the sign faces (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 2 and 3).
questions.question: This sign means Closed to vehicles: no vehicle may pass from either direction.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 4. It is Closed to motor vehicles other than motorcycles, and light road vehicles are not forbidden.
questions.question: On a road with this sign, two-wheeled motor vehicles may pass but other motor vehicles may not.

questions.explanation: This is Closed to motor vehicles other than motorcycles. Every motor vehicle except a two-wheeler is forbidden (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 4).
questions.question: This sign shows that only ordinary passenger cars may not pass.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 5. It is Closed to large goods vehicles etc.; ordinary motor vehicles may pass.
questions.question: This sign shows that large goods vehicles, large special motor vehicles and the like may not pass.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 7. Motor vehicles other than two-wheelers, and light road vehicles, are not forbidden.
questions.question: On the road where this sign stands, ordinary motorcycles, large motorcycles and general motorized bicycles (mopeds) are all forbidden to pass.

questions.explanation: This sign is Closed to motorcycles and general motorized bicycles, and neither two-wheeled motor vehicles nor mopeds may pass (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 7).
questions.question: The vehicles this sign closes the road to are only two-wheeled motor vehicles, so a general motorized bicycle (moped) may travel on that road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 10. A combination closed-to-vehicles sign forbids the combination of vehicles pictured on it; vehicles not pictured may pass.
questions.question: This sign shows that only the kinds of vehicle pictured on it may not pass.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 12. It is No entry except in the direction indicated: you may not go any other way.
questions.question: At an intersection with this sign, a vehicle must not go in any direction other than the one the arrow shows.

questions.explanation: This is No entry except in the direction indicated. The One way sign is a blue rectangle with a white arrow, and is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 12 and 31).
questions.question: This sign shows that the road is one way.

questions.explanation: This is No entry except in the direction indicated, and the signal must still be obeyed. You may turn left on red or yellow only where there is a "Left turn permitted" plate (Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4)).
questions.question: At an intersection with this sign you may go in the direction of the arrow even when the light ahead is red.

questions.explanation: The arrow shows straight ahead only, so neither a right nor a left turn is allowed (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 12).
questions.question: At an intersection with this sign a vehicle may turn right or left as well as go straight on.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 13. A crossing that involves a right turn is forbidden even to enter premises off the road.
questions.question: Where this sign stands a vehicle must not cross the road, except for a crossing that involves a left turn in order to enter or leave premises off the road.

questions.explanation: Only crossing the road is forbidden. U-turns and reversing are not forbidden by this sign (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 13).
questions.question: Where this sign stands, U-turns and reversing are forbidden as well as crossing the road.

questions.explanation: This is No crossing by vehicles, and what is forbidden is crossing the road. A right turn at an intersection is not forbidden (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 13).
questions.question: This sign shows that right turns are forbidden.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 14. It is No U-turns: you may not turn round and go back the way you came.
questions.question: This sign shows that vehicles are forbidden to make a U-turn.

questions.explanation: Only U-turns are forbidden; a right turn is not (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 14).
questions.question: In the stretch where this sign stands, a vehicle may not make a U-turn and may not make a right turn at an intersection either.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 15. Overtaking without crossing into the right-hand part is not forbidden by this sign alone.
questions.question: On a road with this sign, a vehicle must not cross into the right-hand part of the road to overtake.

questions.explanation: This is No crossing into the right-hand part of the road to overtake. To forbid overtaking itself, a "No overtaking" auxiliary sign is added (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 15 and 16).
questions.question: This sign shows that overtaking itself is forbidden.

questions.explanation: Because the "No overtaking" auxiliary plate is fitted, overtaking itself is forbidden, whether or not you cross over (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 16 and 80).
questions.question: Where this sign and its auxiliary plate stand, you may overtake as long as you do not cross into the right-hand part of the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 17. Even stopping to let someone in or out is not allowed.
questions.question: This sign shows that both parking and stopping are forbidden.

questions.explanation: This is No stopping or parking, and stopping is not allowed either. The sign that forbids only parking is No parking (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 17 and 18).
questions.question: Where this sign stands, stopping to let someone in or out is allowed.

questions.explanation: This is No parking. Passing is not forbidden; parking is (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 2 and 18).
questions.question: Where this sign stands, a vehicle may not even drive through that road at all.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 75. It is fitted below a main sign such as No parking and shows that the restriction begins here.
questions.question: This auxiliary sign shows the start of the section in which the main sign's restriction applies.

questions.explanation: This is the auxiliary sign for the start of the section. The one for the end has its arrow the other way (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 75 and 77).
questions.question: This auxiliary sign shows the end of the section in which the main sign's restriction applies.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 77. Beyond it, the main sign's restriction no longer applies.
questions.question: This auxiliary sign shows the end of the section in which the main sign's restriction applies.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 24. Maximum width is judged on the width including the load.
questions.question: This sign shows that a vehicle whose width, load included, exceeds the figure shown may not pass.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 25. A general motorized bicycle (moped) may not exceed its own lower limit of 30 km/h either.
questions.question: On a road with this sign, neither motor vehicles nor streetcars (trams) may be driven faster than the speed shown.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 26. You must not drive slower than the speed shown.
questions.question: This sign shows that a minimum speed is set for motor vehicles.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 30. Vehicles may not pass, except those specially permitted, such as a vehicle with a garage along the road.
questions.question: The road where this sign stands is for the exclusive use of pedestrians and the like, so no vehicle may enter it except one specially permitted to pass.

questions.explanation: This sign marks a road for pedestrians and the like; apart from specially permitted vehicles, vehicles may not pass at all (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 30).
questions.question: This sign shows that many pedestrians use the road, so a vehicle need only pass with care.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 31. It is One way: you may travel only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.question: A driver who spots this sign must not move the vehicle in the direction opposite to the one the arrow points.

questions.explanation: This is the One way sign. The "Left turn permitted" plate shows that you may turn left even when the light ahead is red or yellow, which is a different meaning (Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 2 item 1(4)).
questions.question: This sign means the same as the "Left turn permitted" plate.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 35. It is Lane use by direction, and you must travel according to the division shown.
questions.question: When approaching an intersection with this sign, a vehicle must travel according to the lane division that matches the direction it is going.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 35-2. You go straight to the far side of the intersection, change direction there and then go on.
questions.question: At an intersection with this sign, a general motorized bicycle (moped) must turn right by the two-step method.

questions.explanation: Where the "Sound horn" sign stands you must sound the horn. Proceeding slowly is not a substitute (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(5)).
questions.question: Where this sign stands, it is enough to proceed slowly (徐行) without sounding the horn.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 40. A stop required by the sign is a duty, however safe it may look.
questions.question: Where this sign stands, a vehicle must come to a complete stop (一時停止) even when there is no other traffic and it plainly seems safe.

questions.explanation: This is the note to Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). Where there is no stop line, the stopping position is just before the intersection.
questions.question: Where this sign stands, a vehicle stops just before the stop line if there is one.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 items 7(5) and 7(6). Leave the tramway promptly or keep well clear of the streetcar.
questions.question: On a road with this sign a motor vehicle may drive on the tramway, but when a streetcar (tram) comes up from behind it must not obstruct it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 55. While travelling on a priority road you have no duty to proceed slowly (徐行), even at an intersection with poor visibility.
questions.question: This sign shows that the road you are travelling on is a priority road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 59. Vehicles may not enter a safety zone.
questions.question: The place where this sign is set up is a safety zone, so a vehicle must not enter it.

questions.explanation: This is an indication sign showing a pedestrian crossing. A school, kindergarten or the like is shown by a yellow diamond warning sign (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 57 and 182).
questions.question: This sign shows that there is a school, a kindergarten or the like nearby.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 182. A child may also step out from behind a parked vehicle, so slow down as you pass.
questions.question: On a road with this sign there is a school, a kindergarten or the like nearby and children may run out, so you must drive with particular care.

questions.explanation: This is a warning sign telling you there is a school, kindergarten or nursery nearby. A pedestrian crossing is shown by a different sign (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 57 and 182).
questions.question: This sign shows that there is a pedestrian crossing ahead used by schoolchildren.

questions.explanation: This is a warning sign telling you the road surface is slippery. The crosswind sign shows a windsock and is a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 184 and 194).
questions.question: This sign warns you to watch out for a crosswind.

questions.explanation: It is a warning sign that calls for care; it does not forbid passing (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 185).
questions.question: This sign shows that, because of the risk of falling rocks, you may not pass beyond it.

questions.explanation: This is a warning sign telling you the number of lanes is reduced. A narrowing road is shown by the Road narrows sign, a different one (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) items 188 and 189).
questions.question: This sign tells you that the road narrows ahead.

questions.explanation: It is a warning sign telling you there are road works and calling for care; it does not forbid passing (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 193).
questions.question: A driver who sees this sign must not take the vehicle any further, because road works are going on ahead.

questions.explanation: You may use it when pulling over to the edge or the centre of the road to make a right or left turn, and when road works or the like leave you no choice. It is not the case that you may never use it (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 33 and Chapter 5, Section 2, item 6(2)).
questions.question: On a road where this sign designates an exclusive lane for route buses, etc., an ordinary motor vehicle may never use that lane, whatever the circumstances.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 33. Pulling over to the edge or the centre of the road to make a right or left turn, and cases such as road works where there is no choice, are exceptions.
questions.question: On a road where this sign designates an exclusive lane for route buses, etc., every vehicle other than small-sized special motor vehicles, motorized bicycles and light road vehicles (bicycles, carts, etc.) may not travel in that lane.

questions.explanation: This is an exclusive lane, so you may not use it even if you intend to leave when a bus comes up. The lane you may stay in and leave promptly when a bus approaches is the priority lane (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 33 and Chapter 5, Section 2, item 6(2)).
questions.question: In an ordinary motor vehicle, you drove in the exclusive lane for route buses, etc. designated by this sign, intending to leave it once a route bus came up.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 25. It is the Maximum speed sign, and you may not drive faster than the speed it designates.
questions.question: When you enter a road carrying this road sign in an ordinary motor vehicle, the driver must hold the speed so that it does not go above 40 km/h.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 25. It is the Maximum speed sign, and the figure on it is the maximum speed designated.
questions.question: This road sign shows that the maximum speed on the road ahead is designated as 60 km/h.

questions.explanation: A general motorized bicycle may not be driven at more than 30 km/h. A maximum speed sign designates a speed for a general motorized bicycle only when the speed shown is 30 km/h or less (Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 1(2) and Appendix 3(1) item 25).
questions.question: A person riding a general motorized bicycle (moped) on a road where this road sign stands does not break the maximum speed rule even by working the speed up to 50 km/h.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 35-3. The sign designates the small right turn for general motorized bicycles, and in that case the rider may turn right on a green arrow light.
questions.question: At an intersection on a road with this sign, a general motorized bicycle (moped) must move over as close to the centre of the road as it can beforehand and turn right just inside the centre of the intersection, proceeding slowly (徐行).

questions.explanation: A general motorized bicycle may not carry a passenger at all, whether or not this sign is there (Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 4(1)). What the sign forbids is travel with a passenger by large motorcycles and ordinary motorcycles (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 11).
questions.question: This sign forbids large motorcycles and ordinary motorcycles to travel carrying a passenger, so a general motorized bicycle (moped) may travel on a road with this sign with a passenger aboard.

questions.explanation: This sign designates the two-step right turn for general motorized bicycles, so the rider must move over as close to the left edge of the road as possible beforehand (Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 35-2 and Chapter 8 Section 3 item 3(2)ア). Moving over to the centre of the road is the small right turn.
questions.question: A rider of a general motorized bicycle (moped) about to turn right at an intersection with this sign must move over to the centre of the road and turn while proceeding slowly (徐行) just inside the centre of the intersection.
